title: Theorem Proving in Lean 4
byline: Jeremy Avigad, Leonardo de Moura, Soonho Kong and Sebastian Ullrich · Lean 4 edition
note: This PDF is a browser print of the online book, so it has no table of contents or printed page numbers; chapter ranges here are PDF pages. Sections are not broken out. Each chapter also links to the free online edition on lean-lang.org, which may be newer than this PDF. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: The standard introduction to proving theorems in Lean 4. It teaches the dependent type theory underneath Lean (the Calculus of Inductive Constructions with universes) and uses propositions-as-types throughout: a proof is a term, logical connectives and quantifiers are types, and equality is an inductive family. With that foundation it covers term-mode proofs, tactic proofs, the practicalities of working in Lean, inductive types and recursion (structural and well-founded), structures, type classes, conv mode, and the axioms (propositional and function extensionality, quotients, choice) together with their computational cost.

chapters.title: 1. Introduction
chapters.summary: Computers in proof: automated versus interactive theorem proving, and Lean’s place among them.

chapters.title: 2. Dependent Type Theory
chapters.summary: Lean’s type theory from simple types to dependent types: definitions, variables, sections, namespaces and implicit arguments.

chapters.title: 3. Propositions and Proofs
chapters.summary: Propositions as types: proofs as terms, the logical connectives, and classical reasoning as an extra axiom.

chapters.title: 4. Quantifiers and Equality
chapters.summary: The universal and existential quantifiers, equality, rewriting and calculational proofs.

chapters.title: 5. Tactics
chapters.summary: Building proofs interactively with tactics: intro, apply, exact, rw, simp, cases, induction, and combinators.

chapters.title: 6. Interacting with Lean
chapters.summary: Practical Lean: imports, sections, namespaces, attributes, notation, coercions and settings.

chapters.title: 7. Inductive Types
chapters.summary: Defining inductive types (enumerations, structures, recursive and indexed families) and their eliminators.

chapters.title: 8. Induction and Recursion
chapters.summary: Pattern matching, structural and well-founded recursion, mutual and nested recursion, and dependent pattern matching.

chapters.title: 9. Structures and Records
chapters.summary: Structures as single-constructor inductive types, with projections, inheritance and anonymous constructor notation.

chapters.title: 10. Type Classes
chapters.summary: Type classes for overloading and canonical structures: instances, defaults, outParams, coercions and instance resolution.

chapters.title: 11. The Conversion Tactic Mode
chapters.summary: The conv mode for rewriting inside specific subterms of a goal.

chapters.title: 12. Axioms and Computation
chapters.summary: Propositional extensionality, function extensionality, quotients and choice, and what they do to computation.
